entities.summary: Mile Budak was a Croatian politician and writer best known as one of the chief ideologists of the Croatian fascist Ustasha movement, which ruled the Independent State of Croatia (NDH) during World War II in Yugoslavia from 1941 to 1945 and waged a genocidal campaign of extermination against its Roma and Jewish population, and of extermination, expulsion and religious conversion against its Serb population. He was sentenced to death in 1945 by the post-war communist authorities in Yugoslavia over war crimes and crimes against humanity.
